$comment: Generated from TODO.md by an eight-way classification pass, then ordered by the project rule in TODO.md: lowest-numbered task first, with dependencies enforced. Edit `order` to change what runs first. `runnable: false` tasks are never attempted; the runner prints them as skipped with the reason.

tasks.title: Resolve the size conflict in rendered markdown (mockup 15px/1.65 vs --jp-content-font-size1 14px)
tasks.reason: docs/decisions.md lists this in Still open as blocked on Design — an agent cannot decide which of two authored values wins.
tasks.riskReason: Changes the token surface: font.size.content.1 is the base of the whole content type ramp, and P3-03's entire rendered-markdown surface derives from the winner.

tasks.title: Get Design and Accessibility sign-off on D-002 (ANSI palette narrowing of PRD T4)
tasks.reason: The Done-when is an accessibility sign-off or a rewrite of a written PRD acceptance criterion, which only the Design and A11y owners can give.
tasks.riskReason: No code changes — the arithmetic and the audit implementation already ship; this only ratifies them.

tasks.title: Sign off mapping/jp-adapter.yaml with Design and Engineering (the P0 exit gate)
tasks.reason: The Done-when is explicitly a person reviewing 233 rows one by one and approving them on a PR.
tasks.riskReason: Approval only; the mapping file itself is unchanged by the act of signing it off.

tasks.title: Re-derive the anchors in design-reference/data4now/COMPONENT-INDEX.md
tasks.reason: P0-02 recovered the design file and proved the index is stale: CSS banners after L610 are 76 lines low, body anchors are 103 lines low, and the JS column cites banner comments that are not in the file. Every anchor is verifiable with grep, so an agent can do this unattended.
tasks.riskReason: Edits one reference document. No shipped CSS, no TypeScript, no test changes.

tasks.title: Put the D-021 mark on screen and close the B5 gap
tasks.reason: D-021 decided the mark and P0-07 authored the asset, so the remaining work is mechanical: override ui-components:jupyter in packages/icons/src/manifest.ts, and replace the letter D in the splash tile with the same pie-chart O so PRD B5 holds. Both halves are verifiable in a browser.
tasks.riskReason: Changes the brand mark on two visible surfaces at once, and an unknown LabIcon name fails silently — LabIcon.resolve registers a placeholder rather than throwing.

tasks.title: Galata harness and snapshot baseline
tasks.reason: Fixture wiring, a deterministic font container and a first baseline run are all machine work in the existing container; the Blocked-by task P2-01 (top panel) is already done, so nothing human remains.
tasks.riskReason: Test-only and additive — tests/galata/ holds only configuration today, and committed baselines affect no shipped surface.

tasks.title: Favicon delivery (Q11)
tasks.reason: PRD Q11 is open on Platform for both halves of the Done-when — the delivery route and whether the deployment uses busy-state swapping — and CLAUDE.md lists P1-08 among the tasks blocked on Design/PM rather than engineering.
tasks.riskReason: The hook is the jupyterlab_d4n server extension, which the Jupyter server loads at startup, so a fault there can stop the server rather than just mis-render a tab.

tasks.title: Decide the scope of JupyterLite (Q7)
tasks.reason: PRD Q7 is a PM scope call — supported with a CI job, or documented as unsupported — and the task's Done-when is the recorded decision itself.
tasks.riskReason: Produces a decision record and then either a new CI job or a documentation line; neither touches shipped CSS or plugins.

tasks.title: Menu dropdowns (.lm-Menu) — fixed four-column grid, M1 to M8
tasks.reason: The remaining work is verification, and all of M2 to M8 are browser-checkable with Playwright in the dev container: icon/shortcut/both/neither/submenu items side by side, a menu longer than the viewport, submenu flips at 1280x720, both modes.
tasks.riskReason: menu.css governs every menu in the application because Lumino portals menus into body, so one bad grid template misaligns menus everywhere; §8.4.5 also permits escalating to a custom Menu.IRenderer, which turns a CSS task into a JS one.

tasks.title: Sidebar rails and panel headers
tasks.reason: The remaining CSS and the both-mode measurement need nobody; the authored-at-20px icons are P5-01 manifest/asset work and the task text explicitly allows shipping scaled icons with a written note instead of waiting.
tasks.riskReason: Extends one theme-gated stylesheet (sidebar.css, already taking the rail width from --d4n-sidebar-rail-width so no private variable is touched); the icon half changes no shipped CSS.

tasks.title: Dock tab bar — teal current-tab border, dirty dot, close affordance, split handle
tasks.reason: What remains is browser measurement plus a pointer-driven drag of the 8px hit area over the 1px visual, both scriptable; only the subjective 'still feel wrong' caveat is beyond a machine, and it is a caveat, not the Done when.
tasks.riskReason: One stylesheet, already scoped through .lm-DockPanel-tabBar and .lm-TabPanel-tabBar so it cannot leak into the sidebar rails.

tasks.title: Declarative toolbar and menu restructuring through overrides.json
tasks.reason: It is settings-schema authoring plus browser verification, with the composition shape given in PRD §7.6; anything not expressible declaratively is escalated with a note under the working rules rather than decided by a person.
tasks.riskReason: overrides.json recomposes every toolbar and menu in the application: a wrong item name is dropped silently, a disabled menu is a behaviour change users see, and a malformed file takes the settings load down with it — the closest thing in P2 to a start-time failure outside the plugin swaps.

tasks.title: Status bar overflow — collapse at 1024px into a ⋯ popover
tasks.reason: Both branches of the Done when are inside an agent's reach — a public-API plugin on the P2-02 precedent, or dropping the task with a written reason — and D-015 already closed off the swap option, so no tier decision is left for a person.
tasks.riskReason: New shell plugin acting on IStatusBar: statusBar.ts explicitly forbids registering it as an IStatusBar provider, and doing so would shadow core's working bar; the 1024px viewport number is also expected to move the way the menu bar's did.

tasks.title: T3: launcher behavior — section order, root copy, no-kernels state, search
tasks.reason: It is a plugin implementation with a precise Done when (L1 to L9 plus the four behaviours) and needs no sign-off, asset or new visual design — §8.11.5 already specifies the error state copy — though Q3 on the readout is still open with Design and PM.
tasks.riskReason: It must disable @jupyterlab/launcher-extension:plugin in the same commit: two ILauncher providers make JupyterLab refuse to start, and a replacement that misses the launcher:create command id leaves four dead + affordances owned by four other plugins.

tasks.title: Cell container, active-cell indicator, prompts, 24px collapser hit area
tasks.reason: Pure CSS extension of the existing surfaces/notebook.css (102 lines already covers the container, prompts, collapser and .jp-mod-active) plus browser measurement in both modes; nothing here needs a person.
tasks.riskReason: Additive rules in one already theme-gated stylesheet; the worst outcome is a 24px collapser hit area that swallows clicks near the prompt, which is visually obvious and revertable, and cannot affect boot.

tasks.title: Output area, stream output, error output, 2px danger left border
tasks.reason: The error-output plate and border are specified in token terms (danger.subtle plate, 2px danger.default left border) and land in the same notebook.css that already styles .jp-OutputArea-output.
tasks.riskReason: Additive rules in a single shipped stylesheet on tokens that already exist; no plugin, no token source and no boot path is touched.

tasks.title: Rendered markdown (.jp-RenderedHTMLCommon) type ramp, tables, code, lists
tasks.reason: The task says to settle P0-08 first, and P0-08 is the unresolved 15px-vs-14px call that decisions.md lists as blocked on Design, so an agent cannot start the ramp without deciding it by fiat.
tasks.riskReason: Resolving it means writing font.size.content.1 in the token source, which changes the token surface and cascades through --jp-content-font-size1 into every rendered output; it also adds the largest single CSS surface in scope.

tasks.title: Wire the generated ANSI block into rendermime and verify T2
tasks.reason: generated/ansi.css already ships through packages/tokens/style/index.css into ui-overrides, so what is left is specificity checking plus the T2 comparison of `ls --color=always` in a terminal and a cell, both of which an agent can drive in the browser.
tasks.riskReason: Mostly verification; any code change is an import or a selector in generated-adjacent CSS, and the generated file itself is rebuilt by the freshness gate rather than hand-edited.

tasks.title: CodeMirror 6 theme and HighlightStyle across eleven languages
tasks.reason: Fixture authoring and tag-coverage testing are engineering work; the six StreamLanguage languages have no kernel in the dev image, but a fixture that declares language_info drives the editor mode without one, so no person is needed.
tasks.riskReason: It rewrites the HighlightStyle and theme object that every editor and every notebook cell mounts; a malformed extension or a bad tag list makes editors render unstyled or throw on open, and the design lints do not inspect a JS theme object.

tasks.title: Terminal bridge — all four triggers, T1 to T10
tasks.reason: terminalBridge.ts is built and already registered as @d4n/shell-chrome:terminal, so this is test-led work (theme-then-open, 20 consecutive switches) that an agent can run against the container.
tasks.riskReason: Contained to xterm options for terminal widgets; a regression hands the palette back to core's `inherit` object per D-004 but touches no other surface and cannot stop the app starting.

tasks.title: Autocomplete popup, inline signature, tooltip, console panel
tasks.reason: Four surfaces with existing token coverage; no decision, asset or sign-off is called for in the task text.
tasks.riskReason: The completer and the tooltip portal outside the shell into body, so a wrong position, size or stacking rule can cover the editor and block typing — a failure the contrast and selector gates would pass.

tasks.title: Wire CM6 breakpoint gutter and execution-line decorations to the debugger
tasks.reason: debugDecorations.ts (413 lines) is written and inert by design; the remaining work is mapping DAP breakpoints and the stop event onto its effects, and ipykernel in the dev image ships debugpy so an agent can drive a real session.
tasks.riskReason: It activates a gutter and a StateField inside every editor the debugger attaches to; a faulty effect or range set throws inside CodeMirror at stop time, and D4's contrast gate against every syntax token is easy to regress silently.

tasks.title: Debugger panel shell, callstack, breakpoints, sources, empty states
tasks.reason: PRD §8.6.1 and §8.6.3 give the geometry and the exact empty-state copy ("No breakpoints set", "Not paused", "No sources"), so nothing must be invented; note the overlap with P5-05, which IS flagged as net-new design work for other panels.
tasks.riskReason: A new panel-scoped stylesheet plus generated empty-state content; confined to the debugger sidebar and revertable, though the empty states put English strings into CSS content, which a reviewer may want to relocate.

tasks.title: Debugger variables tree view
tasks.reason: The task removes the only judgement call itself — value colours must reuse the existing color.syntax.* tokens rather than new choices — leaving row geometry and states an agent can measure.
tasks.riskReason: Additive CSS on one sidebar section using tokens that already exist and are already audited; no JS, no plugin and no token source involved.

tasks.title: T3/T4: DataGrid — apply buildGridStyle and buildTextRenderer to both grids
tasks.reason: Both factories already exist in packages/shell-chrome/src/gridStyle.ts and the wiring plus the plugin disable is engineering, not a decision.
tasks.riskReason: It disables a core plugin (@jupyterlab/csvviewer-extension:csv) in page_config.json in the same change; if the replacement misses the document-widget factory or the file-type registration, CSV and TSV files stop opening for every user, and the same D-015/D-016 trap applies where the disabled plugin's schema survives.

tasks.title: Notebook search overlay and the other five search mounts
tasks.reason: S1's "one component, six configurations" is a consolidation job against stable class names, with the base input already partly in inputs.css; the S4 and S5 behaviours are testable in a browser without a person.
tasks.riskReason: S1 forces the change into the shared inputs.css that all six mounts consume, so one regression hits the command palette, file-browser filter, settings search and extension-manager search at once; the overlay also floats over the document where a bad offset can occlude the first cell.

tasks.title: ipywidgets — variables in compat-shim, sliders, file upload, repaint
tasks.reason: CSS plus a stale-inline-style check that an agent can verify by rendering widgets, switching theme and re-reading the DOM; ipywidgets is absent from the [dev] extra but the agent can install it in the container to test.
tasks.riskReason: It edits compat-shim's vendored ipywidgets stylesheet and the --jp-widgets-* mapping, which repaint every widget in every output area, and those variables sit deliberately outside the audited adapter so the token lints give less cover than elsewhere.

tasks.title: Decide the opt-in helper for matplotlib and Vega (Q5)
tasks.reason: The task word is "Decide" and decisions.md lists Q5 as owned by PM and needed by P3 exit, so an agent producing a helper would be manufacturing a scope decision that content is an explicit non-goal.
tasks.riskReason: Whatever is produced is a decision record or an opt-in package that ships nothing into the interface; the danger is scope creep and a fabricated PM decision in docs/decisions.md, not a broken build.

tasks.title: RJSF global CSS pass against the stable class names
tasks.reason: No human blocker — RJSF's class names (.form-group, .field-string, .field-boolean, .array-item, .control-label, .field-description) are stable and an agent can extend packages/settings-forms/style/settings-forms.css and measure the result in a running settings editor in both modes; note the task carries NO 'Done when' clause, so the runner must treat PRD §7.7's ~85% coverage as the bar.
tasks.riskReason: It is the single stylesheet every RJSF field in the settings editor depends on, so one wrong global rule degrades every settings form at once, and reaching spec is likely to need new Tier-3 token groups (no checkbox/radio/switch/settings groups exist in components.tokens.json today).

tasks.title: Settings editor shell, plugin list and JSON view
tasks.reason: No human blocker — the design source exists (`.jp-SettingsEditor` banner at L1608 of `design-reference/data4now/JupyterLab Theme.html`), the surfaces are plain CSS, and the JSON view inherits the CM6 theme rather than needing its own.
tasks.riskReason: Additive CSS on one new surface, gated under body[data-jp-theme-name^='Data4Now'] (D-003); it disables nothing, touches no token, and cannot affect application boot.

tasks.title: fieldRenderer: keybinding capture
tasks.reason: No human blocker — the chord-capture interaction is engineering, the key-cap look already exists in the design system (13 `kbd` treatments in the theme file), and `src/renderers/README.md` names the intended registry key `@jupyterlab/shortcuts-extension:shortcuts.shortcuts` and tells the agent to verify it against the running build.
tasks.riskReason: An exception inside an RJSF field takes down the whole settings form, not just that row (stated in renderers/README.md), and a capture listener that leaks swallows keystrokes application-wide; a wrong registry key fails silently with the stock field still rendering.

tasks.title: fieldRenderer: theme picker
tasks.reason: No human blocker — the swatch grid with an `is-on` selected state is already designed in `design-reference/data4now/Form Controls.html` (L860-L870, L1370-L1380), so this is composition against existing tokens rather than net-new design, and the whole point (PRD R5) is that a native <select> popup cannot be themed.
tasks.riskReason: It replaces the control that switches themes; if the renderer throws or the registry key `@jupyterlab/apputils-extension:themes.theme` is wrong, the settings form breaks or silently keeps the stock select, and theme switching is the one interaction every other verification step in this project depends on.

tasks.title: fieldRenderer: editor settings
tasks.reason: No human blocker — grouping the ~15 flat properties of `@jupyterlab/fileeditor-extension:plugin.editorConfig` and mounting a live preview is structural engineering that an agent can build and verify in the browser.
tasks.riskReason: The live preview mounts a CodeMirror instance inside an RJSF field, so a mount or dispose fault takes the whole settings form down with it; it also writes real editor configuration, which is user-visible state outside the settings editor.

tasks.title: fieldRenderer: font picker
tasks.reason: No human blocker — previewing each option in the face it names and filtering to fonts the browser actually has are runtime questions the agent can answer with `document.fonts`, and the `.sel` control is already designed in Form Controls.html.
tasks.riskReason: Additive single-field component, but it shares the documented RJSF hazard that one throw removes the entire settings form; font enumeration also behaves differently in the container than on a host, so a browser-verified pass can still be wrong elsewhere.

tasks.title: fieldRenderer: color picker
tasks.reason: No human blocker — the swatch component is designed in Form Controls.html and the contrast machinery the picker is meant to surface already exists in `tests/contrast/audit.mjs`, so both halves are buildable and verifiable by an agent.
tasks.riskReason: It writes colour strings into live plugin settings (the README names the terminal ANSI overrides as a target), so a bad write is user-visible outside the settings editor, and it carries the same whole-form RJSF failure mode as the other renderers.

tasks.title: All form controls: input, select, checkbox, radio, switch (+ custom listbox for the kernel and cell-type pickers)
tasks.reason: No human blocker — checkbox, radio, switch and select are all designed in `design-reference/data4now/Form Controls.html` (`.chk/.rad/.sw/.sel`), and PRD R5 already prescribes the custom listbox for the two high-traffic pickers, so nothing here is left to a person to decide.
tasks.riskReason: The custom listbox replaces the kernel picker and the cell-type picker — two core notebook affordances — so a fault ships an instance where the user cannot change kernel or cell type; and checkbox/radio/switch have no component tokens today, so reaching spec means adding to the Tier-3 token surface.

tasks.title: Dialogs, toasts, tooltips and progress, plus the focus contract
tasks.reason: No human blocker — tooltip tokens already exist and the tooltip, dialog, notification and progress treatments all have design anchors in the theme file, and the task itself tells the agent to test whether core already satisfies the focus contract before writing anything, which is exactly a browser measurement.
tasks.riskReason: It extends several shipped stylesheets at once (dialog.css, notifications.css, plus new tooltip and progress rules) and, if core's focus trap turns out to be insufficient, adds keyboard behaviour to a modal overlay where a mistake can trap focus with no way out.

tasks.title: Decision point: does the settings editor reach spec, or does it need a T3 replacement of settingeditor-extension:form-ui?
tasks.reason: The task is labelled a Decision point and asks whether to spend a contingency scoped in PRD R2 — a judgement about product quality against cost that a person must make, and the task body says to take it at the P4 exit rather than at ship.
tasks.riskReason: The yes-branch disables `@jupyterlab/settingeditor-extension:form-ui` and re-provides it; on the D-015/D-016 precedent a swap that misses a surviving command id or settings schema leaves dead affordances, and an incomplete replacement leaves the application with no working settings editor.

tasks.title: Complete the icon override manifest from the P0-04 audit
tasks.reason: docs/icon-manifest.md records 65 registry names as NEEDS AUTHORING with no Data4Now asset behind them, so I1 ("no stock glyph left on a surface we own") cannot be reached until a designer draws those glyphs — and the task itself forbids guessing a name to fill the gap. D-020 adds the menu half: 160 rows across 152 commands, most of which have no LabIcon to override, so they are declared through overrides.json and therefore wait on P2-12.
tasks.riskReason: Icon overrides change the glyph on every owned surface at once, and a wrong registry name is not an error: LabIcon.resolve registers a placeholder under it, so the mistake is silent and also poisons that name for the next extension.

tasks.title: Review the icon contact sheet for consistent optical weight (I3)
tasks.reason: I3 is a human optical-weight judgement made across a whole sheet, and the only remedy for a failure is redrawing icons, which is net-new visual design.
tasks.riskReason: The deliverable is a finding, not a code change; nothing ships from it directly.

tasks.title: Apply the motion tokens with a prefers-reduced-motion branch on every consumer
tasks.reason: The task describes a sweep plus a lint, both of which are code the agent can write and verify; motion.css already carries the blanket reduced-motion guard and dialog.css, launcher.css, settings-forms.css and splash.ts already carry local ones, so the work is finding and fixing the stragglers.
tasks.riskReason: Applying motion tokens per consumer edits several shipped stylesheets, and adding a sixth lint to the lint:design chain can fail the whole gate for files nobody expected it to touch.

tasks.title: Compact density (D-009) wired through the chrome, with the terminal bridge re-fit
tasks.reason: D-009 already settled the approach, the density.compact.* tokens exist in components.tokens.json and packages/shell-chrome/src/density.ts already observes data-d4n-density and emits the signal the terminal bridge needs — what remains is the toggle command, its settings binding, persistence and the CSS, all measurable in the browser.
tasks.riskReason: It re-dimensions control heights across many shipped stylesheets, adds a settings key and a new plugin, and drives trigger (c) of the terminal bridge, so a mistake is visible on every surface at once.

tasks.title: Empty, loading, error, permission-denied and offline states for every panel
tasks.reason: The task says outright that this is new design work and not restyling — the copy, the illustration and the layout for five states on every panel have to be designed first, and PRD §6.7 confirms JupyterLab ships blank or text-only for most of them.
tasks.riskReason: Rendering a state where core renders nothing means replacing panel plugins rather than styling them, and a swap that re-provides a token core still provides can stop JupyterLab starting — the failure mode P2-15 records for ILauncher.

tasks.title: Table of contents panel (PRD §8.10)
tasks.reason: PRD §8.10.1 specifies the six-level ramp row by row (size, weight, indent, colour) and the toc.level1..6 tokens already exist, so levels 4-6 are a token application rather than a new design decision; no TOC stylesheet exists yet, so the surface is a clean additive write.
tasks.riskReason: One new stylesheet plus its selectors.json rows, scoped to the TOC panel; the exposure is that TC7's tree semantics (role, aria-level, aria-expanded) may not be reachable from CSS and would have to be reported rather than forced.

tasks.title: Full accessibility audit, A1 to A13
tasks.reason: A5 to A13 are manual by definition in PRD §9 — a keyboard sweep, a prefers-contrast check, a 200% zoom pass and an NVDA/Firefox plus VoiceOver/Safari screen-reader pass — and AC7 requires the accessibility owner to sign the result off.
tasks.riskReason: The deliverable is an audit record; no shipped code changes as part of the task itself.

tasks.title: Third-party compatibility matrix, P0 and P1 rows, both modes, with Galata snapshots
tasks.reason: Installing the P0/P1 extensions, writing the compat CSS and capturing snapshots is all machine work and packages/compat-shim already holds the scaffold plus three vendor stylesheets — but the "dedicated Galata snapshots" half needs the harness and baseline that P1-07 delivers.
tasks.riskReason: It adds vendor stylesheets to a shipped package and installs third-party extensions whose own JupyterLab pins can move the version in the dev image, which would break every later task's environment.

tasks.title: Performance budgets (PRD §10.5) gated in CI
tasks.reason: Every budget in §10.5 has a stated machine method — Playwright trace for TTI and scroll fps, performance.mark around the theme switch, bundle analyzer for gzipped CSS, heap snapshot for memory delta — so the agent can build the harness and the CI job without a human in the loop.
tasks.riskReason: New measurement scripts and a CI job; nothing that ships to the browser changes.

tasks.title: Upgrade playbook (Appendix C), documented and rehearsed against a real minor bump
tasks.reason: Appendix C step 4 requires every regenerated Galata snapshot diff to be reviewed and approved by a person (§10.1 repeats this), and step 8 is the manual QA pass, so the agent can write the playbook but cannot close the rehearsal that AC11 asks for.
tasks.riskReason: A rehearsal moves the JupyterLab version pin, which can break selectors, fail the adapter completeness check and leave the application unable to start — and it does so across the whole repo, not one surface.

tasks.title: Manual QA scenarios 1 to 9, both modes (PRD §10.6)
tasks.reason: All nine scenarios are browser-drivable in the container the same way every earlier task in this repo was verified, and none of them asks a person to decide, approve or supply anything — the word "manual" describes the method, not a sign-off gate.
tasks.riskReason: Verification only, no shipped code change; the real hazard is a false green, so any scenario the harness cannot genuinely drive (pointer feel, ANSI colour by eye) must be reported as skipped rather than passed.

tasks.title: Packaging check: pip install jupyterlab_d4n && jupyter lab (AC1)
tasks.reason: Building the wheel, installing it into a clean container and booting JupyterLab to confirm the redesign appears with no manual configuration is a scripted end-to-end check the agent can run and measure.
tasks.riskReason: Verification; any fix lands in packaging metadata (pyproject, install.json, the shipped overrides) that the existing build job already exercises.

tasks.title: Test AC10 end to end — stock theme plus arbitrary extension install
tasks.reason: Switching to a stock theme and installing an arbitrary extension are both actions the agent can perform in the running container and measure; D-003's theme-name gate is the thing under test and it is already implemented.
tasks.riskReason: Test-only; a failure is a report about the gate, not a blind patch to it.

tasks.title: Decide whether to send the accessibility contrast fixes upstream to JupyterLab core (Q8)
tasks.reason: Q8 is an engineering-lead call about contributing to an external project — the decision and its record are the deliverable, not code.
tasks.riskReason: At most a decision entry in docs/decisions.md; nothing in the product changes.

tasks.title: Pilot: 20 daily users or more, one week, zero P0 bugs (AC13)
tasks.reason: AC13 needs 20 real people using the build for a week and a satisfaction score from them; an agent can neither run a pilot nor accept its result.
tasks.riskReason: No code change; the outcome is a report that gates the release.
